features.name: Upstream atelier's monorepo-aware hooks into templates, then sync the stale copies in hangar and atelier
features.description: T2 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-two-layer-harness-design.md. feat-075's baseline found hangar 2 and atelier 6 drifted hooks, in both directions: atelier's py-guard and ts-guard (2026-10-13) gate on the files changed since the upstream merge-base, show the failing output and fix tsc -b --noEmit (TS6310), while the templates still run whole-repo; ts-fix hard-codes atelier's app. sh-check, yaml-validate, migration-guard and ruff-fix are older in the repos (sh-check lacks agy support; the rest differ only in header comments). Move atelier's behaviour into templates/hooks with the app folders in the repo config block (APP_DIRS, '.' for a single-app repo), then copy every drifted template into hangar and atelier keeping each repo's config block.
acceptance_criteria: templates py-guard and ts-guard run only for an app folder in APP_DIRS whose files changed against the upstream merge-base (tracked edits, untracked files, and committed-but-unpushed commits all count), and exit 0 when none did; APP_DIRS=('.') treats the repo root as the app
a missing tool prints SKIP and does not block; a failing tool blocks with exit 2 and shows its output
ts-fix formats a file with the prettier of the APP_DIRS folder that holds it, and does nothing for a file outside every folder
scripts/tests/test_shared_hook_templates.sh covers the above and failed before the template change
after the sync, repo_audit.py reports 0 drifted hooks for hangar and atelier, and atelier's config block keeps its app folders
hangar ./init.sh and atelier ./init.sh (their hook tests) pass, or a failure is shown to be pre-existing
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.verification: bash scripts/tests/test_shared_hook_templates.sh && python3 scripts/repo_audit.py ../hangar && python3 scripts/repo_audit.py ../atelier && bash scripts/harness-verify.sh
features.evidence: Templates python/py-guard.sh, js/ts-guard.sh and js/ts-fix.sh now carry atelier's behaviour (turn scope against the upstream merge-base, failing output shown, plain tsc -b) with the app folders in a repo config block APP_DIRS ('.' = repo root); py-guard prints SKIP for each missing tool. scripts/tests/test_shared_hook_templates.sh 37 passed; the 16 new cases failed 6 before the change (whole-repo runs, no output shown, ts-fix ignoring folders). A mutation that drops ts-guard's folder prefix is caught. Writing ts-fix's test found a real bug in my first version: on macOS git prints /private/var/... while the hook got /var/..., so the folder never matched; the hook now compares physical paths. test_init_repo.sh 16 passed. shellcheck clean. Synced with a one-off script that keeps each repo's config block: hangar sh-check, yaml-validate (924ef3f); atelier sh-check, migration-guard, ruff-fix, py-guard (APP_DIRS apps/firstdigital-api), ts-guard and ts-fix (apps/firstdigital) (0b278d1). repo_audit: drifted hangar 2 -> 0, atelier 6 -> 0 (docs/telemetry/repos/*/2026-10-18.json). hangar test-hooks.sh 33 passed and ./init.sh exit 0; atelier test-hooks.sh 32 passed and ./init.sh exit 0. harness-verify.sh: all 11 gates passed, output saved to a file. Not done: harness/guards py-check, secret-scan and sh-check still differ from templates/hooks (this repo's own guards; outside T2). Atelier's hook messages now name the folder (apps/firstdigital-api) instead of the app name. Neither repo commit is pushed.

features.name: install.sh records the installed harness version
features.description: T3 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-two-layer-harness-design.md. Nothing records which harness commit a machine runs, so a target repo cannot tell whether its hook copies or settings match what is installed. install.sh (and so update.sh) writes <runtime dir>/harness-version.json: full and short commit, git describe (tags when present), whether the tree was dirty, and the install time. Later tasks (agent-harness.json, preflight) compare against it.
acceptance_criteria: record_harness_version in scripts/_lib.sh writes harness-version.json with commit equal to git rev-parse HEAD, short, describe (a tag when HEAD is tagged), dirty true only with uncommitted changes to tracked files, and installed_at
outside a git checkout it writes commit null with a reason and prints a warning instead of failing the install
the file is valid JSON for any repo path (spaces, quotes)
install.sh calls it once; a real install on this machine writes the file with the current HEAD
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.evidence: scripts/_lib.sh record_harness_version writes <runtime dir>/harness-version.json (commit, short, describe, dirty, installed_at; outside git: commit null, reason, a WARN, install continues); install.sh calls it once after install_runtime_dir. scripts/tests/test_record_harness_version.sh 10 checks; it failed 9 of them before the function existed. The repo path in the test holds spaces and quotes; JSON is written by python3, which install.sh already requires. Real install: bash scripts/install.sh exit 0, ~/.agent-skills-setup/harness-version.json commit 1a23b64 = git rev-parse HEAD, dirty false. harness-verify.sh: all 11 gates passed, output saved to a file. Not done: no tags exist yet, so describe prints the short commit; the dirty check covers tracked files only (untracked files are not part of an install).

features.name: agent-harness.json: schema, checker, and the files for hangar and atelier
features.description: T4 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-two-layer-harness-design.md (D1: JSON, so macOS system Python 3.9 reads it). A target repo declares for the harness, not the agent: the harness commit it was synced to, its state files, its verify commands, and its hooks in wiring order, each a shared template (templates/hooks/<stack>/<file>) or a repo-local file, with event edit or stop. Explicit hook lists, not whole stacks, so a sync never adds a hook a repo did not choose (common/ also holds grype-guard and pr-guard, which neither repo uses). scripts/harness_adapter.py check <repo> validates it and reports the version against harness-version.json. D6 provisional: hangar keeps no feature_list.json; its file declares AGENTS.md and PROGRESS.md only.
acceptance_criteria: check exits 0 for a valid file and 2 with one line per problem for: missing file, invalid JSON, wrong schema_version, unknown or missing key, wrong type, a hook naming neither template nor local or both, an event other than edit/stop, a template not under templates/hooks, a local hook or state file that does not exist, an empty verify list
check reports the version as in sync, differs (both commits named) or unknown (no harness-version.json) and never fails on it
hangar and atelier get agent-harness.json whose hook lists match their current .claude/settings.json exactly (same files, events and order); check passes for both
runs on macOS system Python 3.9; mypy and ruff clean
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.verification: python3 -m pytest tests/test_harness_adapter.py -q && python3 scripts/harness_adapter.py check ../hangar && python3 scripts/harness_adapter.py check ../atelier && bash scripts/harness-verify.sh
features.evidence: scripts/harness_adapter.py check <repo> validates agent-harness.json (schema_version 1; harness {source, version}, project {name}, state_files, verify, hooks [{template|local, event edit|stop}] in wiring order) and reports the version against harness-version.json as in sync / differs (both commits) / unknown without failing. tests/test_harness_adapter.py 17 passed. Tests and code were written in the same step, so the tests did not fail first; instead four mutations were run: unknown keys allowed, version always in sync and template+local both allowed were each caught; dropping the stays-under-templates/ check survived, because the test's ../escape.sh did not exist and failed for the wrong reason; the test now creates that file and the mutation is caught. Runs on /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6; mypy and ruff clean. hangar (8 hooks, 0cd1eb8) and atelier (10 hooks, 8c4ec32) files were generated from their .claude/settings.json, so files, events and order match; check passes for both, version in sync (1a23b64). Both ./init.sh exit 0 with the new file. D6 taken provisionally: hangar declares AGENTS.md and PROGRESS.md only (no feature_list.json), as today. harness-verify.sh: all 11 gates passed, output saved to a file. Not done: nothing reads verify or hooks yet (T6, T8); the explicit hook list replaces the stacks idea in the design, because common/ also holds grype-guard and pr-guard which neither repo uses.

features.name: Hook drift is checked against the harness templates, not between sibling repos
features.description: T5 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-two-layer-harness-design.md, with D2 changed: the per-repo values stay in each hook's repo config block (they are bash: arrays, regexes, $REPO_ROOT paths; moving them to JSON needs an eval loader in every hook), and that block stays the only part a repo may edit. What caused the drift was comparing hangar with atelier instead of with the harness. harness_adapter.py drift <repo> [--file F] compares each template hook listed in agent-harness.json with its template outside the config block. New shared hook templates/hooks/common/harness-drift.sh runs it on edit, finding the harness through harness-version.json (now also recording source_dir); with no harness installed (top2, vm1 clones) it does nothing. hangar drops shared-hook-drift.sh and its tests; its nightly security-check.sh compares both repos with the harness.
acceptance_criteria: harness-version.json records source_dir, the harness checkout that was installed

drift exits 0 when every listed template hook matches its template outside the repo config block, and 2 naming each file and its template otherwise; --file limits it to one file and exits 0 for a file that is not a listed template hook

harness-drift.sh blocks (exit 2, message on stderr) an edit that makes a template hook differ, allows an edit inside the config block, ignores other files, and exits 0 when harness-version.json or its source_dir is missing

hangar: shared-hook-drift.sh, its settings.json wiring and its test-hooks.sh cases are gone; harness-drift.sh is wired on edit in hangar and atelier settings.json and agent-harness.json; hangar docs/hooks.md and security-check.sh compare with the harness
hangar and atelier ./init.sh pass; harness_adapter.py check and drift pass for both
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.verification: bash scripts/tests/test_record_harness_version.sh && python3 -m pytest tests/test_harness_adapter.py -q && bash scripts/tests/test_shared_hook_templates.sh && python3 scripts/harness_adapter.py drift ../hangar && python3 scripts/harness_adapter.py drift ../atelier && bash scripts/harness-verify.sh
features.evidence: D2 changed (design doc): per-repo values stay in each hook's repo config block, the only part a repo may edit; copies are compared with their templates, not with each other. harness_adapter.py drift <repo> [--file F] compares each template hook listed in agent-harness.json with .claude/hooks/<name> outside the block (one _strip_config, imported from repo_audit). New templates/hooks/common/harness-drift.sh runs it on edit; it finds the harness through harness-version.json, which now records source_dir. Tests failed first: test_record_harness_version.sh (source_dir) 1 failed, tests/test_harness_adapter.py 3 failed, test_shared_hook_templates.sh 5 failed (hook missing); now 11 checks, 20 passed and 42 passed. Live: a non-config line appended to hangar's real sh-check.sh is blocked with exit 2 naming common/sh-check.sh; the clean copy exits 0. hangar 53a5aae: shared-hook-drift.sh, its wiring and its test-hooks.sh case 7 (sibling pair) removed, harness-drift.sh wired; security-check.sh now runs harness_adapter.py drift for hangar and atelier and alerts if agent-skills-setup is missing; docs/hooks.md updated. atelier 78fb190: harness-drift.sh wired (settings.json edited in its one-line style; my first json.dump rewrite reformatted the whole file and was reverted). drift: none for both; check passes, version in sync (3bc81d3). Both ./init.sh exit 0. The first full gate run failed test_init_repo.sh: profile full must copy every template and init-repo.sh lists common hooks by name; harness-drift.sh added there (16 passed). Second run: all 11 gates passed, output saved to a file. Not done: harness-drift.sh reads ~/.agent-skills-setup only, so a harness installed under another .skills-repo-id is not found (the hook then does nothing); security-check.sh's new block was checked by bash -n, shellcheck and the same commands run by hand, not by running the nightly job.
